questions.q: When payment terms are set at both the supplier level and the supplier site level, which value does Oracle actually apply on an invoice?
options: Always the supplier-level value
Whichever was entered first, regardless of level
An average of the two
The site-level value, because it is more specific and overrides the supplier-level value
questions.explain: When a supplier site has its own value, that site-level value overrides the supplier-level default for invoices entered against that site.

questions.q: In the Alpine Trail Gear ticket, what was the actual root cause of invoices defaulting to Net 30?
options: The supplier-level payment terms were set incorrectly
The specific supplier site used on these invoices had its own incorrect Net 30 override, despite the supplier level correctly showing Net 60
The clerk manually typed Net 30 on every invoice
The contract itself specified Net 30
questions.explain: The supplier record correctly showed Net 60, but the site-level override of Net 30 took precedence, which was the actual source of the wrong default.

questions.q: After correcting the supplier site's payment terms, what happens to invoices that were already entered under the wrong Net 30 terms?
options: They are automatically updated to Net 60
They are automatically deleted
They remain unaffected by the setup fix and must be corrected individually
They are placed on hold automatically
questions.explain: A setup fix changes defaults for future transactions only — it is not retroactive, so each already-entered invoice needs to be corrected individually.

questions.q: Why is it a mistake to consider this ticket resolved after only fixing the supplier site setup?
options: Because invoices entered before the fix still carry the wrong payment terms and remain wrong until corrected individually
It isn't a mistake — fixing the setup is always sufficient
Because the supplier site cannot actually be corrected
Because setup changes require Oracle support approval
questions.explain: The setup fix only prevents the issue going forward; every invoice already entered under the incorrect terms needs its own correction.

questions.q: What is a likely explanation for why the supplier site had the wrong payment terms in the first place?
options: Oracle assigns random payment terms to new sites
The AP manager changed it on purpose
Payment terms cannot be set at the site level, so this was a system error
The value was likely copied from a template or another supplier during setup and never corrected
questions.explain: The lesson notes this kind of mismatch commonly comes from copying setup values from a template or another supplier without updating them for the new supplier's actual contract.
